summary: Client header-based version lock lost during canary health-probe wave causing unexpected fallback to degraded variant
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that tenant-scoped 'X-Model-Pin' header set by their client is inconsistently honoured during a staged canary window. Instead of routing to the pinned model variant, traffic intermittently falls back to the degraded fallback variant during a health-probe surge from internal canary probes. Impact: Several production requests returned degraded-model outputs for short bursts (~30-60s), causing downstream NovaHealth inference scoring to drop and one downstream job to fail validation checks. Environment: prod-us-east, tenant: novahealth-prod, model route: /v1/generate (pinned via header). Occurrence: first observed 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC; recurring during canary health sweep at ~09:12–09:17 and again at 13:45. Hypothesis: Edge smoothing / circuit-shedding combined with asynchronous commit of header-based pin creates a window where the orchestrator's staged-commit path bypasses the pin and applies fallback policies when probe-induced prewarm/drain events cause ephemeral re-routing.

Operational ask: Confirm root cause and provide mitigation (hotfix or recommended client-side change) and a short-term workaround for NovaHealth to avoid production impact while fix is deployed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sets X-Model-Pin: gpt-large-v2-quantized in request header when calling /v1/generate
2) Trigger a staged canary by incrementing canary weight to 10% in us-east for the canonical route
3) Run a health-probe wave (internal) configured to prewarm and then probe 50 edge nodes in quick succession
4) Observe routing logs: some requests from the pinned tenant are routed to fallback variant instead of pinned model for ~30-60s windows
5) Repeat with lower probe concurrency and observe that issue frequency decreases

Possible race where header-pin is not applied for in-flight requests if snapshot merge occurs between edge sticky lookup and commit confirmation. Proposing a guard during staged commit: treat header-pin as higher priority until commit is confirmed.

investigation_notes: Reproduced locally in staging by simulating 40 concurrent health probes hitting edge-proxy + orchestrator; when prewarm ack latency >300ms commit-path sometimes chooses fallback route due to slot-marking logic.

Edge-proxy sticky lookup occurs before orchestrator epoch merge. If orchestrator snapshot update completes after edge sticky read but before commit ack, header-based pin state can be lost for in-flight requests.
Observed related condition: sidecar backpressure and circuit-shedding triggers 'slot-unavailable' which immediately applies fallback variant without re-evaluating header pins for pending requests.
Log correlation: request-ids abc124 and abc128 show identical timing where orchestrator logged 'slot-unavailable' within 8–12ms after edge read.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: customer to include explicit model field in request body and temporarily increase client retry/backoff to avoid hitting the probe window. Engineering proposed patch: change orchestrator commit flow to mark header-based pin as 'sticky-until-ack' so in-flight requests keep the pin even if snapshot merge occurs; also add a short (500ms) debounce for health-probe bursts to avoid back-to-back prewarm-induced drain. Patch PR opened and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/842. Estimated deployment to canary next 48 hours pending review. Follow-ups: - add automated test for header-pin retention across snapshot merges - update canary health probe config to include smoothing defaults

3) SRE to adjust health-probe smoothing if necessary
4) Support to coordinate with NovaHealth on deployment window and temporary mitigation rollback
